cands.name: James T. Martin
cands.bio: Democratic nominee, 33, fourth-generation Floridian. Coast Guard Academy graduate (2015); about 10 years of service rising to captain, including commanding a cutter in Fort Pierce. Chief of staff for national security affairs under then-Vice President Kamala Harris, 2021-2025. Has not held elective office. Won the primary by 362 votes.

record.text: Priorities: cost of living, clean water (restore Lake Okeechobee's natural flow), property insurance (federal backstop for Citizens), ban on congressional stock trading, quarterly town halls.
Won the Aug 18 Democratic primary 50.4% to Bernard Taylor's 49.6% (24,054 to 23,692).

money_notes.text: Has raised $772,560, about 73% in-state, accepts no PAC money, and put $150,000 of his own money into the campaign (WLRN voter guide, Oct 2026).

endorsements.text: Kamala Harris, state Rep. Debra Tendrich, Palm Beach County Tax Collector Anne Gannon (Florida Politics via Wikipedia); Moms Demand Action 'Gun Sense' candidate and End Citizens United 'Unrig' candidate; several Democratic caucuses (WLRN).

cands.gaps: No usable photo: the campaign site image URL needs a signed link (plain URL returns 403). Wikipedia describes him as a Coast Guard Reserve lieutenant commander; WLRN says he rose to captain after about 10 years of service, so rank is not stated.

cands.name: Brian Mast
cands.bio: Republican, U.S. House since 2017 (sixth-term bid). Army Reserve bomb-disposal technician who lost both legs to an IED in Afghanistan in 2010 (Bronze Star, Purple Heart). Chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee since January 2025; also on Transportation and Infrastructure. District 21 now covers Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties plus Jupiter and Palm Beach Gardens.
cands.local_ties: Lives in Fort Pierce; raised in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

record.text: Chair, House Foreign Affairs Committee (since Jan 2025); Transportation and Infrastructure Committee member.
Introduced three water-quality bills in 2025 that remain in House committees (per WLRN voter guide).
Co-sponsored a Sept 2025 bill letting the Secretary of State revoke passports of Americans who criticize Israel, then filed an amendment removing that provision (per Wikipedia).
Redistricting: his seat now takes in Indian River County and gives up some inland Palm Beach County territory.

money_notes.text: Campaign accounts held $4.9 million as of Oct 17, 2026; PACs gave $1.2 million (57.5% from ideological Republican/pro-Israel, transportation and defense PACs); about two-thirds of contributions from out of state.

Earlier-cycle donors cited by Wikipedia include Duty Free Americas and Amway/Alticor; he also took thousands from Igor Fruman (later charged with campaign finance violations) and said he believed the money was donated to charity.

controversies.text: Business Insider reported late STOCK Act disclosures of stock transactions in 2021 and 2022 (Virgin Galactic, Ideal Power, Aphria/Tilray).
Nov 1, 2023 remark that 'very few innocent Palestinian civilians' exist; repeated similar comments to protesters in Feb 2024.
Aug 2020: apologized for 2009 and 2011 Facebook posts he called 'disgusting and inappropriate'.
2016: linked to an advisory-board role at World Patent Marketing, a company the FTC shut down; Mast said he had no knowledge of the company's practices.

foreign_ties.text: Volunteered with the Israel Defense Forces civilian program Sar-El in 2015; wore an IDF uniform in Congress after the Oct 2023 attack (Wikipedia).

endorsements.text: Donald Trump, U.S. Chamber of Commerce, NFIB, Animal Wellness Action, Combat Veterans for Congress, Campaign for Working Families (WLRN voter guide); AIPAC (Wikipedia).
